---
title: "DNA Origami Hybrid Nanopores"
subtitle: "Published research"
---

Programmable DNA-origami nanostructures can be incorporated into solid-state nanopores to create a hybrid sensing interface.

## Research question

How do nanoscale confinement, device geometry, and DNA–protein interactions affect protein capture and translocation signals?

## Approach and contributions

I engineered hybrid nanopores incorporating DNA origami and conducted ionic-current measurements of holo-human serum transferrin. The work compared open solid-state and DNA-origami hybrid nanopores and quantitatively analyzed current blockade, translocation duration, and event characteristics.

## Research scope

The published study reports enhanced sensitivity for protein translocation measurements. The complete methods, results, and limitations are available in the peer-reviewed paper.

## Publication and cover

[Joty et al., Analytical Chemistry (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.4c02016).
